meta.title: DigiBoom. We'll explode your sales. In a good way.
meta.description: Selling on Etsy alone? DigiBoom opens your Shopify and Gumroad storefronts for you, moves your catalog across and keeps everything in sync, so your work gets found in more places than one. Join the early access list.
meta.ogAlt: DigiBoom. We'll explode your sales. In a good way.

hero.headline:
We'll explode
your sales.
<accent>In a good way.</accent>
hero.paragraph: You sell your templates, presets, brushes and fonts on <mark>Etsy</mark>. Only Etsy. One shelf, one shop, and you already know how that story goes. DigiBoom opens your other storefronts on <mark>Shopify</mark>, <mark>Gumroad</mark> and the rest, then keeps every listing in sync. More places to be found. More buyers. None of the extra hours.
hero.signupNote: Free early access for the waitlist. Product updates, nothing else. We have no interest in cluttering your inbox.

product.heading: You bring one shop. We open the rest.
product.intro: Most sellers list in one place. The ones who grow list in three or four. That is three or four times the storefronts a buyer can trip over you on, for a sliver of the work. DigiBoom does the expanding. You approve each step, we do the rest.

features.title: Be where the buyers already are
features.text: Opening a store used to cost you a week you did not have, so you never bothered. We handle the account, the branding, the categories, the fine print. You are live on a new marketplace by dinner, in front of people who have never heard of you.

features.title: Every listing lands ready to sell
features.text: Files, descriptions, variants, tags, licences. All of it travels with the product, shaped to fit each platform, not just the title and a price. Nothing to re-upload. Every new store is open for business on day one.

features.title: More stores, not more hours
features.text: Change a price once. Ship a new version once. Every storefront catches up in seconds. The busywork that used to swallow your week is simply gone, so you can go as wide as you like and keep your evenings.

syncPanel.footRight: 3× the places buyers can find you

problem.heading: One shop, one audience, one bad day from zero

cards.title: A second store costs weeks
cards.text: New account. New branding. New categories. Then every file and description, re-uploaded by hand. Most people start this and quietly give up.

cards.title: One marketplace, one audience
cards.text: Your work is only ever seen by people already on that one platform. Everyone shopping the others has no idea you exist.

cards.title: Every change, done twice
cards.text: New version, new price, new tags, times every platform you are on. Hours a week spent producing nothing at all.

how.heading: From one shop to a storefront network

steps.title: Connect your shop
steps.text: Point us at the store you already run, Etsy or Shopify or Gumroad, through the official API. Pull the plug whenever you feel like it.

steps.title: Import your catalog
steps.text: We read your listings, your files and all the fiddly metadata, then work out what fits where.

steps.title: Open new storefronts
steps.text: Guided setup on the platforms you are missing. Account, branding, categories, policies, mostly filled in before you touch a thing.

steps.title: Publish everywhere
steps.text: Your catalog arrives at every new store intact. Files, copy, tags, licences. You upload nothing twice.

how.payoffText: Same catalog, several times the shelf space, in front of every marketplace instead of the one you started with.

payoff.heading: Then the orders come from everywhere
payoff.paragraph: Your catalog goes live across every marketplace you sell on. Each one is another place a stranger trips over your work. Each one keeps selling while you make the next thing. One upload, working in every direction at once. <accent>That is the boom.</accent>
payoff.note: Reach is the lever we hand you. Three or four times the storefronts, none of the busywork. What you do with it is your business.

platforms.heading: Every place digital goods sell
platforms.intro: Marketplaces put you in front of new buyers. Your own stores let you keep the margin. Do both. Etsy, Shopify and Gumroad come first, then we keep adding, in the order early members actually ask for.

items.q: Do I need stores on the other platforms already?
items.a: No. That is the entire point. If Etsy is all you have, we walk you through opening the rest, fill in most of the setup for you, and carry your catalog over.

items.q: Can it open the accounts entirely on its own?
items.a: No, and you would not want it to. The marketplaces make you accept the terms and prove who you are, yourself. We prepare everything around those two steps. Branding, categories, policies, listings, files.

items.q: Is this against the marketplace rules?
items.a: No. We use the official public APIs with OAuth, the same doors these platforms open to any app developer. No scraping. No handing us your password.

items.q: Do you keep my files and customer data?
items.a: Your data stays yours. Files sit encrypted, only for as long as a sync needs them, and you can export or wipe the lot whenever you want.

items.q: When can I actually try it?
items.a: The first build, Etsy and Shopify in sync, goes to a closed beta. Waitlist members get in first, in the order they signed up. Join now, thank yourself later.
Roman Travnikov. Founder and lead developer, ten-plus years shipping on the web, building DigiBoom out in the open. The whole plan is in the white paper.
